fields.claim_quote:
It follows that $\forall n \in \Z$: 
:$ 2\pi n < x < 2\pi n + \pi$
fields.explanation: The source literally quantifiesforallintegern after assumingtan(x/2)≠0. Keepx=pi/2,n=1;tanpi/4=1,sinx=1, but2pi<pi/2 fails. Actual Real.pi,Real.tan,Real.sin and positivepi prove premise and strict-order failure.
fields.flaw: The proof claims that tan(x/2) ≠ 0 implies, for every integer n, 2πn < x < 2πn + π.
fields.problem:
Title: Primitive of Cosecant Function/Tangent Form/Proof 1

:$\ds \int \csc x \rd x = \ln \size {\tan \frac x 2} + C$
where $\tan \dfrac x 2 \ne 0$.
fields.source_context:
0001 | Since:
0002 | :$\tan \dfrac x 2 \ne 0$
0003 | 
0004 | It follows that $\forall n \in \Z$: 
0005 | :$ 2\pi n < x < 2\pi n + \pi$
0006 | 
0007 | So:
0008 | :$\csc x + \cot x \ne 0$
0009 | 
0010 | And:
0011 | :$\dfrac {1 + \cos x} {\sin x} \ne 0$ 
0012 | 
0013 | Hence:
0014 | {{begin-eqn}}
0015 | {{eqn | l = \int \csc x \rd x
0016 |       | r = -\ln \size {\csc x + \cot x} + C
fields.witness: Take x = π/2 and n = 1. Then x/2 = π/4, so tan(x/2) = tan(π/4) = 1 ≠ 0. The claimed instance is 2π < π/2 < 3π. Its left inequality is false because π > 0 implies π/2 < 2π; the right inequality is true.
